findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil request
findings.body: ContextualLoggerMiddleware in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go dereferences req without a nil check, e.g. req.PluginContext in QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics. LoggerMiddleware in the same package explicitly guards with if req == nil, proving nil requests are considered possible. Because CreateMiddlewares orders ContextualLogger outer to Logger, a nil request panics in ContextualLogger before it can reach Logger's guard, crashing the plugin request path instead of passing through.

findings.title: MetricsMiddleware panics on nil request
findings.body: MetricsMiddleware in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go dereferences req without a nil check, e.g. req.Queries in QueryData and req.PluginContext / req.Body in CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics. LoggerMiddleware guards if req == nil, showing nil is expected. Since MetricsMiddleware is ordered outer to LoggerMiddleware, a nil request causes a nil-pointer panic in metrics code before Logger's guard is reached.

findings.title: Plugin request log loses traceID correlation
findings.body: LoggerMiddleware in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go previously added traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext to the Plugin Request Completed log. The PR removes that logic and the replacement instrumentContext in contextual_logger_middleware.go only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname, never traceID. As a result the backend-request log can no longer be correlated to traces, breaking trace-to-log queries and dashboards that relied on the traceID field.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards log observations
findings.body: TestLogger.FromContext in pkg/plugins/log/fake.go returns a brand-new TestLogger instead of the receiver. LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info, so with the fake the Info/Warn/Error call is recorded on a throwaway instance while the original instance under test still shows zero Calls. Tests asserting on the injected logger cannot observe the log, causing false negatives and hiding regressions in log content.
